checklist.text: REVISED SCOPE (investigated 2026-08-22): refraction needs buf:scene.color as a DEPENDENT read, which water's own drawable cannot do (same-pass read is undefined behaviour) — src/graph/passes.js's own note on surface.water says this pass stays 'seam' specifically until this rung. This is a pass-graph flip (seam -> live), not a shader-only change. Steps below reflect the real scope.

New subsystem (water-refraction-subsystem.js): a single half-resolution, screen-sized render target that captures buf:scene.color, scissored to water's current on-screen rect, once per frame, AFTER geometry.world finishes writing it. One-frame latency by design (the Testament's own accepted cost) -- water's tier-5 shader reads LAST frame's capture, never this frame's. DONE 2026-08-22: world-anchored (no camera-delta math -- capturedRect + positionWorld remap instead), target sized/bucketed to the body/view intersection (Law 6, specular-surface-subsystem.js's own precedent), 33 real tests (state machine + real TSL graph construction against the vendored THREE bundle), full water suite green (601/601).

Wire the subsystem into vt-pan-viewer.js's frame loop, positioned AFTER runGeometryWorldPass (not beside the sim/flow/body prep block, which runs BEFORE the draw) -- this is the actual 'real producer' location the pass-graph flip convention expects (see pass-seams.js's comments on the 5 prior flips, each pointing at 'a viewer closure... see graph/pass-impls.js'). DONE 2026-08-23: runWaterRefractionCapturePass (per-floor, mirrors the sim-tick factory pattern exactly), registered in passImpls['surface.water'], stale-floor disposal wired alongside sim/flow/body. Frame ORDER is the frame-graph's own job (array position in passes.js), not manually placed -- confirmed via graph/__tests__/run-frame.test.mjs, not assumed.

Flip surface.water: status 'seam' -> 'live' in passes.js (add buf:scene.color to reads, declare the new capture resource in creates), remove the 'surface.water': buildWaterPass entry from pass-seams.js's PASS_SEAMS, delete the throwing door in water-pass.js -- matching the exact pattern of the 5 prior flips, never leaving a dead door beside working code. DONE 2026-08-23: also added buf:scene.depth to reads (a pre-existing, previously-undeclared read tier 0 already makes); the new capture resource is deliberately NOT declared as a graph resource (same reasoning res:waterBody/res:waterSim already established -- a same-pass, cross-FRAME producer/consumer has no honest reads-before-creates shape). New PASS_IMPLS entry added (mechanically required, pass-impls.test.mjs enforces exact coverage). validatePassGraph + the full graph suite (282/282) + the full repo suite (11,874) all green.

Tier 5 TSL shader block in water-render.js, at the pre-existing landing strip (search 'TIERS 5-8 -- NOT YET BUILT'): offset screen UV by field.slope x thickness (reuse tier 2's existing slope, no new fetch), sample the new capture texture (remapped via the same uViewRect-based explicit UV technique water already uses for buf:scene.depth, never the shared screenUV() builtin -- feedback_shared_texture_node_carries_the_wrong_uv), validate against buf:scene.depth's rank (fall back to centre UV if occluded), chromatic fringe (+/-1 texel R/B split) gated to the top tier only.

Manifest: add tier 5 to WATER.tiers (n:5, name:'refraction', fromProfile:'quality', cost.class:'C5', estMsPerMp: an honest estimate, flagged unmeasured) and remove it from deferredRungs. While touching deferredRungs: also remove 'reflection' -- docs/holy/Water-Testament.md Sec3.6 (the newer, locked, authoritative ladder) explicitly deletes it from the plan; the manifest's deferredRungs still lists it from the older Water.md ladder, a real drift worth fixing since this array is already being edited.

Tests: extend water-render.test.mjs's tier-construction loop ([0,1,2,3,4] -> include 5) with a stub capture texture input and a structural gate assertion (a refractionCompiled-style boolean or direct node-null check, matching the existing bodyTexNode/normalCompiled pattern) -- STILL OPEN, tied to the shader block itself (previous item). New water-refraction-subsystem.test.mjs: DONE (33 tests). pass-seams.test.mjs / pass-impls.test.mjs needed NO edits -- confirmed by actually running them, not assumed: both are generic/data-driven (walk PASS_SEAMS/PASS_IMPLS/PASSES directly), so the seam removal + new PASS_IMPLS entry were validated automatically. Also fixed two real, unrelated-looking test breaks the live flip surfaced: run-frame.test.mjs's exact frame-order string (surface.water now genuinely appears in it), and a chart-room test that assumed zero judgements would ever graduate to 'done since judged' -- pass:surface.water just became the first one ever, on real data, proving that anti-drift mechanism actually works.

Bench via tools/shader-lab/bench-water.js and the full water test suite; final confirmation is Ingram's own eyes in live Foundry, per the covenant -- this checklist item is 'ready for your look', never 'done' on its own.
